name: Perform Color Deconvolution on Histology Image
description:
You have access to Fiji with a histology sample image.

Your task is to perform color deconvolution to separate different stains:

1. Open a sample histology image:
   - Go to File > Open Samples > HeLa Cells (1.3M, 48-bit RGB)
   - This is a fluorescence microscopy image of HeLa cells

2. Apply Color Deconvolution:
   - Go to Image > Color > Colour Deconvolution (note British spelling)
   - In the dialog, select a built-in stain vector (e.g., 'H&E' or 'FastRed FastBlue DAB')
   - Click OK to perform the deconvolution
   - This will create a new composite window showing the separated color channels

3. The deconvolution creates 3 separate images:
   - Colour_1 (first stain component)
   - Colour_2 (second stain component)
   - Colour_3 (residual)

4. Save the first color channel:
   - Click on the 'Colour_1' image window to select it
   - Go to File > Save As > PNG...
   - Save to ~/Fiji_Data/results/channel_1.png

5. Save the second color channel:
   - Click on the 'Colour_2' image window to select it
   - Go to File > Save As > PNG...
   - Save to ~/Fiji_Data/results/channel_2.png

6. Measure statistics on channel 1:
   - Click on 'Colour_1' to make it active
   - Go to Analyze > Measure (or press Ctrl+M)
   - In the Results window, go to File > Save As
   - Save to ~/Fiji_Data/results/channel_1_stats.csv

Expected Results:
- Two separated color channel images (channel_1.png and channel_2.png)
- Statistics CSV for the first channel
- The deconvolved channels should show distinct staining patterns

Success Criteria:
- channel_1.png exists and is valid
- channel_2.png exists and is valid
- channel_1_stats.csv exists with measurement data

metadata.application: Separating multiple stains in histology images
